selected.title: [A.R. Tucker (Bark) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Daniel L. Ricketson, kept by Annie Holmes Ricketson, on voyage 2 May 1871 - 18 Oct. 1874],
selected.description: Journal of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, desertions, interactions with natives, a death at sea, and taking on provisions at various ports of call. Also contains whale stamps, ship stamps, and accounts. This journal was kept by the Captain's wife and includes detailed descriptions of life at sea, the meals eaten while onboard, and the scenery of varioius ports of call. The crew celebrated the Fourth of July in 1871 with a special dinner and saw "rockets" in the sky. The keeper gave birth to her daughter on 29 August 1871 but died two days later, with a post-mortem photograph was taken of the child before she was put in her coffin. One man was drunk on October 6, 1871. The keeper visited with the Dabney family in October 1871. The vessel began leaking in December 1871. One man fell overboard and drowned on January 29, 1872.; Kendall Whaling Museum (KWM 22); Whaling vessel, out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Daniel L. Prolific English writer; assisted Alexander Mackenzie in preparation of Voyages , 1801 ( Dictionary of National Biography ). // Mackenzie, Roderick: d.1844. Fur trader; cousin of Sir Alexander Mackenzie; brother of Henry MacKenzie (Wallace, Dictionary of Canadian biography ). // After the preface there follow 132 pages on the history of the fur trade in the North West. Some authorities think this was written by his cousin, Roderick MacKenzie. According to the Dictionary of National Biography , Voyages , 1801, was compiled by William Combe from Mackenzie's notes. selected.description: Logbook, kept by William F. Allen, relating to two whaling voyages. First voyage partially documents the Sunbeam (Bark) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by George W.J. Moulton, from 25 July 1882 - 11 June 1886 to the Atlantic and Indian Ocean. Includes descriptions of whales seen and taken, desertions, illnesses, and taking on provisions at various ports of call. Also contains. The keeper writes often about the repairs the crew made to the vessel and whaleboats during the voyage. The crew celebrated Christmas Day in 1884 and 1885 with special feasts. One man was discharged on 4 October 1885 after seeing a doctor in Angola (Africa). The keeper reported a scurvy outbreak in March 1886. The crew found stowaways on 31 March 1886 and 2 April 1886. Whaling grounds include the Carroll, Saint Helena, Pigeon, and Tristan grounds. Second voyage documents the Charles W. Morgan (Bark) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by George A. Smith, from 6 October 1886 - 4 November 1887 to the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans and the Sea of Okhotsk. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, and taking on provisions at various ports of call. Also contains drawings of whale flukes. The keeper writes that most of the crew was homesick and seasick early in the voyage. The keeper notes many references breaking out provisions and working on the vessel, including several instances of blacksmithing. One of the boatsteerers was injured with an axe on May 26, 1887. The steward and cook got into a fight on July 12, 1887. The vessel returned to San Francisco (California) on November 4, 1887. Other places represented include the Strait of Tartary (Sea of Japan) and Cape Patience (Sea of Okhotsk). Whaling grounds include the Sea of Okhotsk, Yellow Sea, Coast of Kamchatka, and Japan grounds.

selected.description: Who We Are is the story, in a format that is part textbook and part historical novel, of nine families that blended through marriage and other relationships over many centuries into a current 21st century American family, the family of William Dennis Hendricson, that's me, and my wife, Susan Lienau Hendricson. As these nine families evolved over time, they cross paths with the famous and infamous who are highlighted in the stories told in this book:  Willem Frederic George Lodewijk van der Dussen , a founding father of modern genealogy in Europe and first chronicler of Hendricson family history;  Maarten Schenck Van Nydeggan Hendriksz , one of Europe’s most villainous mercenary soldiers and Lambert Barentse Hendriksz , Holland’s most revered naval hero; Peter Stuyvesant , peg-legged soldier-politician leader of the New Amsterdam colony; legendary pirate of the Caribbean Captain Henry Morgan ; ill-fated Miles Morgan , vanished in the Carolina’s a decade before the Lost Colony of Roanoke; Molly Reeve Webster , the Witch of Hadley, catalyst for the Salem Witch Trials; and her nemesis, scientist, public health champion and witchcraft-monger, Cotton Mather ; the mystic idealist, William Penn, whose political concepts guided Jefferson, Franklin and other founding fathers; George Washington , need I say more; Daniel Boone ; legendary frontiersman; Molly Pitcher , the mythical Revolutionary War heroine; General Daniel Morgan , hero of Saratoga and Cowpens in the Revolutionary War; British General Charles Cornwallis , the most renowned Redcoat commander of the Revolutionary War; Moses Black Harris , famed Mountain Man of the American West; Abner Doubleday, Civil War General and rumored founder of baseball; WZ Ripley , a catalyst for 20 th century White Supremacy dogma; Ernie Davis, Heisman Trophy winning college football player; George Preston Marshall, key founder of the National Football League in the U.S. and ardent segregationist; Howard Cosell , America’s leading sports journalist in the 1970s; John Lewis, prominent U.S. Civil Rights leader; and Shirley Povich , Pulitzer prize winning sportswriter, with guest appearances by other notables including Christopher Columbus , on his first approach to the Americas, Roger Maris , U.S. baseball legend, the rock band Blood, Sweat and Tears, voting rights advocate Evelyn T. Butts , rockabilly and country western star Jerry Lee Lewis , and best-selling author of “On Death and Dying,” Elizabeth Kubler-Ross. However, Who We Are does not center on these luminaries; they make cameo appearances, engaging various family members,  past and present, in unique experiences, or serving as catalysts for societal phenomenon that influenced the lives of these individuals. Instead, Who We Are is about people who did the best they could to build a safe, happy and prosperous life for themselves in America beginning in the 17 th century. The individuals in the nine families who first immigrated to America were average folk, working class for the most part, with no royal connections or inherited wealth to prop them up. Two of the original immigrants came from merchant families that previously had accrued wealth in Europe, but through misfortune, inexplicable decisions, and political turmoil, had drifted so far away from prosperity that America was seen as their only recourse. Other original immigrants were from families that had known only the meager existence of tenant farm labor for generations. The first immigrants in two other families arrived on legal missions as young, unmarried men, and elected to seek their fortune in America rather than return to uncertain futures in Europe. Who We Are tells the stories of the people in these nine families before and after their arrival in America. All families have extraordinary stories, and collectively, these stories shape society. William D. Hendricson February 17, 2025

description: pages cm

The real story of the pirates of the Caribbean. Henry Morgan, a twenty-year-old Welshman, crossed the Atlantic in 1655, hell-bent on making his fortune. Over the next three decades, his exploits in the Caribbean as a privateer in the service of the English became legendary. selected.description: Who We Are. Stories of American Families is a story of nine families that blended through marriage and other relationships over the centuries into a current 21st century family, the family of William Dennis Hendricson, that’s me, and my wife, Susan Lienau Hendricson. As these families evolved over time, they cross paths with the famous and infamous who are highlighted in the stories told in this book: Willem Frederic George Lodewijk van der Dussen, a founding father of modern genealogy in Europe and first chronicler of Hendricson family history; Maarten Schenck Van Nydeggan Hendriksz, one of Europe’s most villainous mercenary soldiers and Lambert Barentse Hendriksz, Holland’s most revered naval hero; Peter Stuyvesant, peg-legged soldier-politician leader of the New Amsterdam colony; legendary pirate of the Caribbean Captain Henry Morgan; ill-fated Miles Morgan, vanished in the Carolina’s a decade before the Lost Colony of Roanoke; Molly Reeve Webster, the Witch of Hadley, catalyst for the Salem Witch Trials; and her nemesis, scientist, public health champion and witchcraft-monger, Cotton Mather; the mystic idealist, William Penn, whose political concepts guided Jefferson, Franklin and other founding fathers; George Washington, need I say more; Daniel Boone; legendary frontiersman; Molly Pitcher, Revolutionary War heroine; General Daniel Morgan, hero of Saratoga and Cowpens in the Revolutionary War; British General Charles Cornwallis, the most renowned Redcoat commander of the Revolutionary War; Moses Black Harris, famed Mountain Man of the American West; Abner Doubleday, Civil War General and rumored founder of baseball; WZ Ripley, a catalyst for 20th century White Supremacy dogma; Ernie Davis, Heisman Trophy winning college football player; George Preston Marshall, key founder of the National Football League in the U.S. and ardent segregationist; Howard Cosell, America’s leading sports journalist in the 1970s; John Lewis, prominent U.S. Civil Rights leader; and Shirley Povich, Pulitzer prize winning sportswriter, with guest appearances by other notables including Christopher Columbus, on his first approach to the Americas, Roger Maris, U.S. baseball legend, the rock band Blood, Sweat and Tears, voting rights advocate Evelyn T. Butts, rockabilly and country western star Jerry Lee Lewis, and best-selling author of “On Death and Dying,” Elizabeth Kubler-Ross. However, Who We Are. Stories of American Families does not center on these luminaries; they make cameo appearances, engaging various family members, past and present, in unique experiences, or serving as catalysts for societal phenomenon that influenced the lives of these individuals. Instead, Who We Are is about people who did the best they could to build a safe, happy and prosperous life for themselves in America beginning in the 17th century. The individuals in the nine families who first immigrated to America were average folk, working class for the most part, with no royal connections or inherited wealth to prop them up. Two of the original immigrants came from merchant families that previously had accrued wealth in Europe, but through misfortune, inexplicable decisions, and political turmoil, had drifted so far away from prosperity that America was seen as their only recourse. Other original immigrants were from families that had known only the meager existence of tenant farm labor for generations. The first immigrants in two other families arrived on legal missions as young, unmarried men, and elected to seek their fortune in America rather than return to uncertain futures in Europe. Who We Are tells the stories of the people in these nine families before and after their arrival in America. All families have extraordinary stories, and collectively, these stories shape society. selected.title: Augustus De Morgan, Polymath: New Perspectives on his Life and Legacy
selected.description: When Augustus De Morgan died in 1871, he was described as ‘one of the profoundest mathematicians in the United Kingdom’ and even as ‘the greatest of our mathematicians’. But he was far more than just a mathematician. Because much of his voluminous written output on various subjects was scattered throughout journals and encyclopaedias, the breadth of his interests and contributions has been underappreciated by historians. Now, renewed interest in De Morgan’s life and work has coincided with the digitization of his extensive library, revealing the extent to which he pioneered and influenced the development of not merely mathematics but also logic, astronomy, the history of mathematics, education, and bibliography. This edited collection celebrates De Morgan as a polymath. Drawing together multiple elements of his activity from a range of publications and archives, its contributors re-assess his academic work, his place in his intellectual environment, and his legacy. The result offers new insight into De Morgan himself as well as the wider circles in which he moved, including his family life.

selected.title: NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) 20160003380: CubeSat Constellation Cloud Winds(C3Winds) A New Wind Observing System to Study Mesoscale Cloud Dynamics and Processes
selected.description: The CubeSat Constellation Cloud Winds (C3Winds) is a NASA Earth Venture Instrument (EV-I) concept with the primary objective to better understand mesoscale dynamics and their structures in severe weather systems. With potential catastrophic damage and loss of life, strong extratropical and tropical cyclones (ETCs and TCs) have profound three-dimensional impacts on the atmospheric dynamic and thermodynamic structures, producing complex cloud precipitation patterns, strong low-level winds, extensive tropopause folds, and intense stratosphere-troposphere exchange. Employing a compact, stereo IR-visible imaging technique from two formation-flying CubeSats, C3Winds seeks to measure and map high-resolution (2 km) cloud motion vectors (CMVs) and cloud geometric height (CGH) accurately by tracking cloud features within 5-15 min. Complementary to lidar wind observations from space, the high-resolution wind fields from C3Winds will allow detailed investigations on strong low-level wind formation in an occluded ETC development, structural variations of TC inner-core rotation, and impacts of tropopause folding events on tropospheric ozone and air quality. Together with scatterometer ocean surface winds, C3Winds will provide a more comprehensive depiction of atmosphere-boundary-layer dynamics and interactive processes. Built upon mature imaging technologies and long history of stereoscopic remote sensing, C3Winds provides an innovative, cost-effective solution to global wind observations with potential of increased diurnal sampling via CubeSat constellation.

selected.title: The class of '65 : a student, a divided town, and the long road to forgiveness
description: viii, 261 pages : 25 cm

"Being a student at Americus High School in 1964 was the worst experience of Greg Wittkamper's life. A member of a nearby Christian commune, Koinonia, Greg was publicly and devoutly in favor of racial integration and harmony. Koinonia's farm goods were boycotted by businesses for miles around, and they were targeted and attacked with bombs and gunfire by the Ku Klux Klan. But Greg did not waver in his beliefs. When Americus High School was integrated, he refused to participate in the insults and violence aimed at its black students. He was harassed and bullied and beaten but stood his ground. In the summer after his senior year, as racial strife in Americus reached its peak, Greg left town. Forty-two years later, in the spring of 2006, a dozen former classmates wrote letters to Greg, asking his forgiveness and inviting him to return for a class reunion. Their words opened a vein of painful memory and unresolved emotion. The long-deferred attempt at reconciliation started him on a journey that would prove healing and saddening. The Class of '65 transcends the ugly things that happened decades ago in the Deep South. This book is also the story of four people--David Morgan, Joseph Logan, Deanie Dudley, and Celia Harvey--who reached out to their former classmate. Why did they change their minds? Why did it still matter to them, decades later? Their tale illustrates our capacity for change and the ways in which America has--and has not--matured in its attitudes about race. At heart, this is a tale about a pariah and the people who eventually realized that they had been a party to injustice. It is a tandem story of a country and its people--angry, fearful, and proud--to make real change"--

selected.title: Señor Nice : straight life from Wales to South America
description: 308 pages, 16 unnumbered pages of plates : 25 cm

"Howard Marks was released from Terre Haute Penitentiary, Indiana, in April 1995 after serving seven years of a twenty-five year sentence for marijuana smuggling. It was time for a change of career. So he wrote two bestselling books, became a sports writer and travel writer, stood as a parliamentary candidate in Norwich North, Norwich South, Southampton Test and Neath, applied to become the country's Drug Czar, and embarked on a long-running, sellout series of one-man shows." "While performing in his home town of Kenfig Hill, he fell among old friends who made extraordinary claims for Welsh culture. Was Elvis really Welsh? Was there really a tribe of Welsh-speaking Native Americans? At the same time his elderly aunt told him of his outlaw ancestry: William Owen, the legendary Welsh smuggler, who had operated for some time in South America and his great-great-grandfather Patrick McCarty, the half-brother of Billy the Kid, who had joined Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid in Patagonia. He decided to explore South America." "His travels took him to Jamaica and Panama in the footsteps of the Welsh buccaneer Henry Morgan; he went to Brazil looking for groups of Welsh settlers so obscure he never found them, although he did succeed in finding his musical idol Jimmy Page; and he searched among the thriving Welsh community in Patagonia for signs of Billy the Kid's half-brother."--Jacket
